parts.text: I'll set up a minimal, dependency-free CommonJS project using the callback `fs.realpath` (present and consistent since Node 4), wrapped with `util.promisify` rather than the newer `fs.promises`/`fs.realpath.native` APIs that vary by version.

Done. Set up a dependency-free CommonJS project:

- `index.js:6` — exports `realpath`, built on the callback `fs.realpath` wrapped with `util.promisify`.
- `cli.js` — `realpath <path>` command-line entry.
- `test.js` — creates a chain of symlinks and asserts resolution to the canonical path.
- `package.json` — `engines.node >=8`, `npm test`.

Why this is version-consistent: `fs.realpath` (callback form) has existed since Node 4, while `fs.promises` (stable only in 14+) and `fs.realpath.native` (added in 9.2, OS-specific behavior) vary across versions. `util.promisify` gives a promise wrapper without those constraints.

Tests pass (`ok`).
